newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Italy's Prodi in Kuwait to discuss economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi in Kuwait to discuss economic ties.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi arrived in Kuwait on Wednesday for a two-day visit to improve economic ties with the Gulf Arab state.
He was welcomed at Kuwait airport by acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah.

"Boosting mutual trade and investment would be among the main topics of discussion during His Excellency's (Prodi's) visit," a Kuwaiti official said. "Strengthening political relations will be another angle of talks."
Prodi is also scheduled to meet the country's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah.
Italy participated in the 1991 U.S.-led offensive that drove Iraq's troops from Kuwait after a seven-month occupation.

"There is potential for increased cooperation between the two countries especially in the oil industry and infrastructure," an official source said. "Italy also has good investment potential for Kuwaiti capital."
A team of 15 business executives team is accompanying Prodi on his first visit to the country since his May appointment. The team consists mainly of oil and energy industrialists, an official said.
The visit "will open new horizons for economic development between the two friendly countries," the official Kuwait News Agency KUNA quoted Prodi as saying in a dispatch from Rome.
Italy was looking for "further development in the fields of industry and investment," Prodi added, according to the agency.

Kuwait's imports from Italy rose 23 percent in 1995 to about $380 million, and 15 percent in the nine months to September 1996. Kuwait's exports to Italy stood at about $10 million in 1995. No comparative figures were available.
Italy's exports to Kuwait are mainly machinery for the oil industry, clothes and leather products.
